entries.title: Swarmish: what happens when agent swarms create language?
entries.summary: Agent swarms build their own productive language, which the authors call Swarmish. Swarms solve a multi-phase collaborative task using only Swarmish. Decoder swarms partly recover it from transcripts, and more task context improves decoding. The test covers one task, one group size, four model families.
entries.analysis: 48-hour hackathon work; narrow setup, but relevant to multi-agent oversight.

entries.title: What Rewarding Misbehavior During RL Does to Character-Trained Models
entries.summary: Character-trained gpt-oss-20b still learns rule-breaking easily under RL. It learns both harmful answers to math-rewritten requests and reward hacking in agentic coding. It learns harmful answers only slightly slower than the baseline.
entries.analysis: Suggests character training gives weak protection against RL pressure.

entries.title: Scattered thoughts on how doing math feels these days
entries.summary: A mathematician describes LLM maths ability moving from toys in 2024 to "holy god" by early 2026. The post records how confusing the shift felt.
entries.analysis: First-hand capability signal from a working mathematician.
